description: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy across three metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—on the MMLU Pro dataset. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," spans from 0.81 to 0.99 and is scaled linearly with regular tick marks. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale. The blue line with square markers, representing Final Accuracy, begins at approximately 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.81 and remains consistently high, fluctuating slightly between 0.85 and 1.0 across the range. The green line with circular markers, representing Initial Accuracy, starts at about 0.55 and shows a general upward trend, rising to approximately 0.95 by an initial confidence of 0.99. The orange line with diamond markers, representing Δ Accuracy, starts at roughly 0.45 and declines steadily, ending near 0.0 at an initial confidence of 0.99. Error bars are present for all three metrics, indicating variability in the measurements.
